description: CE ShipGen Glossary — Naval terms, craft types, and equipment definitions from Cepheus Engine RAW with Mneme Variant annotations.

entries.definition: A heavily armed merchant vessel with visible weapons. Not disguised — openly combat-capable.
entries.ceRaw: Armed merchant cruisers are merchants that carry enough weapons to defend themselves and others.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation subsidized merchants often carry House-supplied weapons. Independent armed merchants are common in pirate zones.

entries.definition: A cruiser with armor exceeding standard limits. Sacrifices speed and payload for survivability.
entries.ceRaw: Armored cruisers trade agility for protection. They can absorb hits that would cripple standard cruisers.
entries.mnemeNotes: Hegemony armored cruisers are called Ironclads. They lead clan charges into enemy formations.

entries.definition: A carrier optimized for planetary assault operations. Drop ships, marine barracks, and heavy vehicle bays.
entries.ceRaw: Assault carriers carry drop ships and landing craft instead of fighters. They are the centerpiece of planetary invasion forces.
entries.mnemeNotes: Hegemony clans prize assault carriers above all other vessels. A clan without one cannot claim major power status.

entries.definition: An armored small craft designed to deliver troops, marines, or boarding parties to hostile targets. Heavy frontal armor, minimal weapons.
entries.ceRaw: Assault shuttles are armored landing craft. They carry troops through hostile fire to board enemy ships or assault planetary positions.
entries.mnemeNotes: The standard tool of marine boarding actions. Most assault shuttles are single-use by design — survival is secondary to mission completion.

entries.definition: A dedicated asteroid mining vessel. Drills, extractors, and onboard refining capacity.
entries.ceRaw: Asteroid miners extract valuable materials from rocks. They are the industrial backbone of frontier economies.
entries.mnemeNotes: Guild asteroid miners are efficient factories. Independent miners are desperate gamblers. Hegemony clans use slave labor.

entries.definition: A small craft optimized for ground attack and anti-ship strikes. Heavy ordnance, minimal dogfighting capability.
entries.ceRaw: Attack craft are bombers and strike platforms. They carry heavy weapons for hitting ground targets and slow ships.
entries.mnemeNotes: Hegemony attack craft are suicide-honor vessels. Federation attack craft are precision strike platforms. House attack craft are mercenary tools.

entries.definition: A capital ship combining heavy armament with high speed. Trades armor for mobility, designed to hunt down enemy cruisers and merchantmen.
entries.ceRaw: A battlecruiser mounts battleship-caliber weapons on a faster, lighter hull. It is a Striker — built to hit hard and run down anything it cannot outfight.
entries.mnemeNotes: Popular with corsair kingdoms and independent admiralties who need a 'fleet in being' without the cost of a true battleship.

entries.definition: The largest dedicated combat vessel designed to absorb and deliver overwhelming firepower. Sacrifices speed and payload for maximum armor and armament.
entries.ceRaw: A battleship is a massive warship bristling with heavy weapons and thick armor. It is designed to engage and destroy other capital ships and withstand tremendous punishment.
entries.mnemeNotes: In the Mneme setting, true battleships are rare outside of the Core Worlds. Most frontier navies operate Heavy Frigates or System Defense Boats instead.

entries.definition: A small craft equipped for breaching enemy ships. Cutting torches, breaching charges, and assault ramps.
entries.ceRaw: Boarding craft are the pirate's best friend. They cut through hulls and deliver troops directly into enemy vessels.
entries.mnemeNotes: Hegemony boarding craft are clan honor weapons. House boarding craft are used by marine regiments. Guild boarding craft are automated drones.

entries.definition: A small craft designed to deliver heavy ordnance to large targets. Slow but devastating.
entries.ceRaw: Bombers carry missiles, torpedoes, and heavy bombs. They are vulnerable to fighters but deadly to ships.
entries.mnemeNotes: Rare in the Frontier. Most bombers are carrier-based. Independent bombers are usually converted cargo shuttles.

entries.definition: A Line Ship optimized for massive cargo or passenger capacity. The civilian equivalent of a fleet auxiliary, carrying the bulk of interstellar commerce.
entries.ceRaw: Bulk transports are large merchant vessels — liners, heavy freighters, and colony ships — designed to move enormous quantities of goods or people.
entries.mnemeNotes: Passenger Liners and Heavy Transports dominate this category. The 1,000 DT Passenger Liner is the classic example.

entries.definition: A dedicated freight small craft. No passenger accommodations, maximum cargo volume.
entries.ceRaw: Cargo shuttles are flying boxes. They exist to move freight from orbit to surface and back.
entries.mnemeNotes: The most common small craft in civilized space. Every station, port, and ship has cargo shuttles.

entries.definition: A fast, heavily armed escort vessel designed to screen capital ships from missile and fighter attack.
entries.ceRaw: Close escorts stay near the ships they protect. They have powerful point defense and enough speed to intercept threats.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation close escorts are standardized. House close escorts are often customized for specific fleet doctrines.

entries.definition: A specialized vessel for transporting munitions, missiles, and ordnance. Heavily armored and partitioned.
entries.ceRaw: Colliers carry the ammunition that keeps a fleet fighting. They are prime targets and heavily protected.
entries.mnemeNotes: Guild colliers are automated. House colliers are escorted by close escorts. Hegemony colliers are clan honor vessels.

entries.definition: A vessel designed to transport colonists and establish new settlements. Self-sufficient for years.
entries.ceRaw: Colony ships carry everything needed to start a new world — people, equipment, seeds, and hope.
entries.mnemeNotes: The Houses fund colony ships to expand their domains. Federation colony ships are democratic expeditions. Hegemony clans do not colonize — they conquer.

entries.definition: A capital-scale cruiser fitted with extensive command facilities, C4ISR suites, and flagship accommodations. Leads task forces and squadrons.
entries.ceRaw: A command cruiser is a cruiser hull expanded to capital size, carrying the fleet command center, flag quarters, and communication arrays.
entries.mnemeNotes: Often the personal command of an admiral or sector lord. In Mneme, Command Cruisers are distinguished by their advanced sensor domes.

entries.definition: A generic term for small starships used for patrol and escort. Often overlaps with Patrol Corvette.
entries.ceRaw: Corvettes are the smallest starships capable of independent jump operations. They patrol, escort, and perform customs duties.
entries.mnemeNotes: In Mneme, Patrol Corvette is the specific classification. Corvette is the generic term.

entries.definition: A fast escort designed for rapid message and light cargo delivery. Maximizes jump range and maneuver drives at the expense of everything else.
entries.ceRaw: Couriers are built for speed. They have powerful drives, minimal crew, and just enough payload for mail, data, or urgent passengers.
entries.mnemeNotes: The Express network and X-Boat relays use Courier-class vessels. In Mneme, 'Express' is the civilian designation.

entries.definition: The workhorse of any navy — balanced speed, armor, and payload. Designed for independent long-duration operations without fleet support.
entries.ceRaw: Cruisers are the backbone of a fleet. Fast enough to scout, tough enough to fight, and large enough to carry sufficient fuel and supplies for extended patrols.
entries.mnemeNotes: The most common Line Ship in the Mneme Variant. Patrol Cruisers and Mercenary Cruisers are especially prevalent in the Frontier.

entries.definition: A small, balanced craft under 100 DT. Capable of atmospheric flight, short-range patrol, and light utility work.
entries.ceRaw: Cutters are general-purpose small craft — larger than a ship's boat but smaller than a shuttle. They can operate independently for short durations.
entries.mnemeNotes: The standard utility craft of the Mneme Frontier. Modular Cutters with interchangeable pods are especially common.

entries.definition: Immobile or limited-mobility defensive installations. Orbital platforms or planetary surface fortifications.
entries.ceRaw: Defense fortresses are not ships — they are installations. They mount the heaviest weapons and thickest armor possible.
entries.mnemeNotes: Guild-built defense fortresses are automated. House fortresses are manned by elite troops. Hegemony fortresses are clan honor posts.

entries.definition: A fast, heavily armed Line Ship with minimal payload. Designed to screen fleets, intercept enemy ships, and deliver torpedo attacks.
entries.ceRaw: Destroyers are fleet escorts and attack craft. They have powerful drives and weapons but limited fuel and accommodations.
entries.mnemeNotes: The classic 'Destroyer' in Mneme corresponds to our Striker archetype — all engines and guns, little else.

entries.definition: A smaller destroyer (400–800 DT) optimized for escort duty. Faster than a frigate, lighter than a line destroyer.
entries.ceRaw: Destroyer escorts bridge the gap between escorts and line ships. They have the speed of a destroyer with the endurance of an escort.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation designation. House navies rarely distinguish destroyer escorts from full destroyers.

entries.definition: A capital vessel optimized for rapid deployment of small craft across interstellar distances. Combines the speed of a Sprinter with the payload of a Support vessel.
entries.ceRaw: Not a standard CE classification — a Mneme innovation for rapid-response carrier groups.
entries.mnemeNotes: A speculative capital design. No known examples exist in the Mneme Frontier as of 1105.

entries.definition: A super-heavy battleship mounting the largest spinal weapons and heaviest armor possible. Represents the pinnacle of the Brawler archetype.
entries.ceRaw: The dreadnought is the ultimate expression of naval firepower — a ship so heavily armed and armored that it can engage entire fleets.
entries.mnemeNotes: Mneme Variant: Only the Terran Mandate and the Zhodani Consulate operate true dreadnoughts. Most polities cannot afford the maintenance cost.

entries.definition: A Mneme Variant system for grading ship components from Budget to Prototype. Higher quality provides bonuses to performance, reliability, or maintenance intervals.
entries.ceRaw: N/A — Mneme homebrew rule.
entries.mnemeNotes: EQS affects everything from drives to computers. A Prototype M-Drive might provide +1G performance but require double the maintenance.

entries.definition: An individual or small-group survival capsule. Ejected from a ship in extremis.
entries.ceRaw: Escape pods are one-use survival capsules. They preserve life until rescue, then are discarded.
entries.mnemeNotes: Standard equipment on all starships. Guild escape pods are automated. House escape pods have beacons that signal House rescue services.

entries.definition: An escort-sized combatant (200–600 DT) with heavy armor and weapons for its size. Patrol and combat optimized.
entries.ceRaw: Escort frigates are heavy combatants in the escort size range. They sacrifice speed for armor and firepower.
entries.mnemeNotes: Mneme distinguishes Escort Frigates (Brawler/Escort) from Heavy Frigates (Brawler/Line Ship).

entries.definition: A small craft for extravehicular activity. Maintenance, repair, and construction in vacuum.
entries.ceRaw: EVA pods are work craft. They allow crew to perform maintenance and repairs outside the ship.
entries.mnemeNotes: Essential for any ship operating far from port. Guild EVA pods are automated. Independent ships use whatever they can afford.

entries.definition: A civilian courier operating on scheduled express routes. Part of the X-Boat or interstellar mail network.
entries.ceRaw: Express vessels carry mail, data, and urgent passengers on fixed schedules. Speed is everything.
entries.mnemeNotes: The X-Boat network uses dedicated express vessels. Private express companies compete for lucrative corporate contracts.

entries.definition: A mobile manufacturing facility. Produces finished goods from raw materials at destination.
entries.ceRaw: Factory ships manufacture goods at the point of need. They eliminate the cost of shipping finished products.
entries.mnemeNotes: Rare. Most factory ships are Guild-operated. A few House factory ships exist for specialized luxury goods.

entries.definition: A 200 DT merchant with Jump-2 capability. Trades higher-value cargo over longer distances than the Free Trader.
entries.ceRaw: Far traders are Jump-2 merchants. They reach markets that Jump-1 vessels cannot, carrying higher-value cargoes.
entries.mnemeNotes: More profitable than Free Trading but riskier. A Far Trader stuck between systems with no fuel is a dead ship.

entries.definition: A reconnaissance Line Ship built around maximum sensor range and jump capability. Sacrifices armor and weapons for speed and stealth.
entries.ceRaw: Scout cruisers and fleet scouts are designed to range ahead of the main fleet, identify threats, and report back before being detected.
entries.mnemeNotes: The IISS uses Scout/Couriers in this role. Military variants mount additional ECM and sensor drones.

entries.definition: A generic combat small craft. Fast, armed, and fragile. The standard space superiority platform.
entries.ceRaw: Fighters are the most common combat craft. They are fast, maneuverable, and deadly in numbers.
entries.mnemeNotes: Every faction operates fighters. Hegemony clan fighters are personalized. Guild fighters are mass-produced drones.

entries.definition: A capital ship whose primary weapon is its embarked craft wing. The centerpiece of a naval task force, capable of projecting power across multiple systems.
entries.ceRaw: Fleet carriers are the largest warships in terms of crew and embarked craft. They carry dozens or hundreds of fighters, bombers, and assault shuttles.
entries.mnemeNotes: The ultimate Support asset. Fleet carriers never operate alone — they are always surrounded by a screen of destroyers and corvettes.

entries.definition: A long-range escort designed for convoy protection and independent patrol. Larger and more self-sufficient than close escorts.
entries.ceRaw: Fleet escorts operate far from the main fleet. They have enough fuel and supplies for weeks of independent operations.
entries.mnemeNotes: The workhorse of Federation anti-piracy operations. Many retired fleet escorts find second lives as Frontier patrol vessels.

entries.definition: A mobile support vessel that maintains squadrons in deep space. Machine shops, spare parts, and engineering crews.
entries.ceRaw: Fleet tenders carry the infrastructure to keep a squadron operational far from base. They are the oilers and repair ships of space.
entries.mnemeNotes: Essential for extended Hegemony clan wars. House fleet tenders are often converted from old merchant hulls.

entries.definition: The iconic 200 DT tramp merchant. Independent operator, speculative cargo, no fixed route.
entries.ceRaw: Free traders are the romantic image of space commerce — independent captains, speculative cargoes, and the freedom of the stars.
entries.mnemeNotes: The most common ship in the Frontier. Every Free Trader captain has a story, a debt, and a gun under the console.

entries.definition: A merchant vessel designed to carry cargo between star systems. Minimal armament, modest drives, maximum hold space.
entries.ceRaw: Freighters are the lifeblood of interstellar trade. They trade combat capability for cargo capacity and fuel efficiency.
entries.mnemeNotes: The most common ship class in civilized space. Free Traders, Far Traders, and Subsidized Merchants all fall under this classification.

entries.definition: In CE RAW, 'Frigate' is often used loosely for escort-sized combatants. In strict Mneme terminology, the Escort-sized Brawler is the System Defense Boat.
entries.ceRaw: The term frigate covers a range of escort and light combat vessels, typically 200-800 DT, armed for patrol and escort duty.
entries.mnemeNotes: Mneme distinguishes between Escort Frigates (Brawler/Escort) and Heavy Frigates (Brawler/Line Ship).

entries.definition: A sub-light vessel designed for multi-generational journeys between stars. A self-contained world.
entries.ceRaw: Generation ships are mobile worlds. Crews live and die over centuries as the ship crawls between stars.
entries.mnemeNotes: Rare and ancient. Some pre-Collapse generation ships still drift between systems, their crews forgotten by the galaxy.

entries.definition: The captain's personal boat. A small craft reserved for the commanding officer and VIP guests.
entries.ceRaw: Gigs are the captain's private craft. They are small, fast, and often luxurious.
entries.mnemeNotes: House gigs are status symbols. A noble's gig is more expensive than some starships. Hegemony clan chiefs ride to battle in armored gigs.

entries.definition: A heavily armed small craft trading speed and agility for armor and firepower. The 'tank' of small craft combat.
entries.ceRaw: Gunboats are small craft built around a heavy weapon — often a turret or fixed mount too large for a standard fighter.
entries.mnemeNotes: Popular with planetary defense forces that cannot afford full starships. A squadron of gunboats can threaten much larger vessels.

entries.definition: A larger cruiser (5,000–9,000 DT) with enhanced armor and firepower. Lower thrust efficiency than light cruisers.
entries.ceRaw: Heavy cruisers are the fleet's heavy hitters. They can engage enemy capital ships and survive punishment that would destroy lighter vessels.
entries.mnemeNotes: The Hegemony builds heavy cruisers as clan flagships. Each carries the war banner of its commissioning clan.

entries.definition: A 20–40 DT fighter with enhanced armor and weapons. Trades agility for survivability.
entries.ceRaw: Heavy fighters carry more armor and weapons than light fighters. They can survive hits that would destroy lighter craft.
entries.mnemeNotes: Hegemony heavy fighters are clan champions. Guild heavy fighters are automated gun platforms. House heavy fighters are piloted by knights.

entries.definition: A Line Ship optimized for armor and firepower over speed. Acts as a mobile fortress capable of holding a system against superior numbers.
entries.ceRaw: Frigates occupy the space between escorts and cruisers. Heavy frigates maximize armor and weapons, accepting reduced agility.
entries.mnemeNotes: Often used as independent system defenders where a full cruiser squadron is unavailable. The 'poor man's battleship.'

entries.definition: A mobile medical facility. Protected by convention. Unarmed or minimally armed.
entries.ceRaw: Hospital ships treat casualties far from planetary medical facilities. They are protected by convention but still need escorts.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation hospital ships are white-hulled and unarmed. House hospital ships carry weapons for defense. Hegemony clans honor hospital ships.

entries.definition: A dedicated food production ship. Grows crops in controlled environments for fleet or colony support.
entries.ceRaw: Hydroponics vessels produce food in space. They are essential for long-duration fleet operations and colony support.
entries.mnemeNotes: Guild hydroponics vessels are automated. House vessels employ agricultural specialists. Hegemony clans disdain them as dishonorable.

entries.definition: A high-performance attack craft designed to destroy enemy small craft and missiles. Fast, armed, and fragile.
entries.ceRaw: Interceptors are the fighters of space combat — small, fast, and deadly. They rely on speed and maneuverability to survive.
entries.mnemeNotes: The classic space superiority fighter. Most interceptiors carry a mix of beam weapons and missiles.

entries.definition: The foundational principle of Mneme naval architecture: every ship design is a trade-off between Speed (S), Armament (A), and Payload (P). No ship can maximize all three.
entries.ceRaw: N/A — Mneme design philosophy.
entries.mnemeNotes: The auto-naming system is built on the Iron Triangle. Understanding a ship's S/A/P ratios reveals its strategic purpose instantly.

entries.definition: The jump drive — a device that creates a bubble of jump space allowing faster-than-light travel. Rated by parsecs jumped.
entries.ceRaw: The jump drive (J-Drive) enables faster-than-light travel. Each letter corresponds to a maximum jump distance in parsecs.
entries.mnemeNotes: Jump drives require hydrogen fuel equal to 10% of the ship's tonnage per parsec jumped. This fuel requirement dominates ship design.

entries.definition: A vessel designed to carry other ships through jump space. Uses external jump grids and grapple frames.
entries.ceRaw: Jump carriers transport non-jump vessels between systems. They are essential for moving monitors and defense boats.
entries.mnemeNotes: Rare and expensive. The Guilds maintain the largest jump carrier fleet, moving their own monitors between contracts.

entries.definition: A dedicated scientific research platform. Extensive labs, sensor arrays, and zero-G facilities.
entries.ceRaw: Laboratory ships are floating universities. They conduct research that cannot be done on planetary surfaces.
entries.mnemeNotes: Guild laboratory ships are state-of-the-art. Independent lab ships are often underfunded and desperate for grants.

entries.definition: A small craft designed for planetary assault. Armored, armed, and capable of delivering troops under fire.
entries.ceRaw: Landing craft deliver troops to planetary surfaces. They are armored against ground fire and armed for self-defense.
entries.mnemeNotes: Hegemony landing craft are sacrificial. Federation landing craft are heavily armored. House landing craft carry noble marine officers.

entries.definition: A generic small cargo craft. The simplest and cheapest form of small craft.
entries.ceRaw: Launches are basic small craft. They move cargo and people short distances.
entries.mnemeNotes: Every port has dozens. They are disposable, replaceable, and essential.

entries.definition: An emergency escape craft designed to evacuate crew from a stricken vessel. Minimal propulsion, maximum survival.
entries.ceRaw: Life boats are emergency craft. They carry survivors until rescue arrives.
entries.mnemeNotes: Regulated by all factions. A ship without enough life boats is not spaceworthy. Hegemony life boats carry weapons for survival.

entries.definition: A Line Ship designed to transport and deploy fighter squadrons and small craft. Carries minimal direct armament, relying on its air wing for combat.
entries.ceRaw: Light carriers are smaller than fleet carriers but still capable of deploying significant fighter wings. They often escort convoys or support planetary assaults.
entries.mnemeNotes: The smallest carrier capable of independent jump operations. In Mneme, Assault Carriers fall into this category.

entries.definition: A smaller cruiser (1,000–3,000 DT) optimized for high thrust-to-mass ratio. Sacrifices payload for speed.
entries.ceRaw: Light cruisers are fast, independent patrol vessels. They scout ahead of the fleet and respond to distress calls.
entries.mnemeNotes: Popular with the Federation patrol corps. House light cruisers often carry a noble officer as political officer.

entries.definition: A 10 DT single-seat fighter optimized for extreme agility. Minimal armor, maximum speed.
entries.ceRaw: Light fighters are the nimblest combat craft. They rely on speed and maneuverability to survive.
entries.mnemeNotes: The classic dogfighter. House light fighters are status symbols for noble pilots. Independent light fighters are cheap and disposable.

entries.definition: A balanced escort-sized vessel with moderate armor, speed, and payload. The multi-role workhorse of small navies.
entries.ceRaw: Light frigates are general-purpose escorts. They can patrol, escort, or perform light combat duties.
entries.mnemeNotes: Popular with independent system defense forces. Many Houses gift light frigates to allied minor worlds.

entries.definition: A small cargo craft designed to ferry goods between orbiting ships and planetary surfaces. Minimal combat capability.
entries.ceRaw: Lighters and launches are the workhorses of orbital logistics. They move cargo and passengers between surface and orbit.
entries.mnemeNotes: Every port has dozens of lighters. They are cheap, ubiquitous, and essentially disposable.

entries.definition: The maneuver drive — a reactionless thruster that provides thrust for normal-space movement and combat maneuvering.
entries.ceRaw: The maneuver drive (M-Drive) provides thrust measured in Gs. It requires no fuel and produces no exhaust.
entries.mnemeNotes: Mneme Variant: M-Drives are classified by letter code (A-N) and performance rating. Small craft use 's' prefixed drives.

entries.definition: A cruiser designed to transport and support mercenary companies. Vehicle bays, troop quarters, and modular mission equipment.
entries.ceRaw: Mercenary cruisers are mobile bases for hire. They carry troops, vehicles, and enough supplies for extended operations.
entries.mnemeNotes: The classic Broadsword-class. Many operate in the Frontier under letters of marque from minor Houses.

entries.definition: A dedicated missile platform. Minimal armor, maximum missile capacity. Designed to saturate enemy point defense.
entries.ceRaw: Missile boats are one-trick ponies — they launch missiles and run. A squadron can overwhelm a much larger vessel.
entries.mnemeNotes: Hegemony clans use missile boats as honor-duel weapons. Guild missile boats are automated drones.

entries.definition: A homebrew rules extension and setting for Cepheus Engine developed by GI7B. Emphasizes asymmetrical warfare, resource scarcity, and the political fragmentation of a post-collapse frontier.
entries.ceRaw: N/A — Mneme is a homebrew variant.
entries.mnemeNotes: The Mneme Variant introduces modified space combat rules, the Equipment Quality Scale (EQS), and a unique naval doctrine focused on patrol corvettes and system defense.

entries.definition: A mobile military installation. Command center, repair facilities, and accommodations for thousands.
entries.ceRaw: Mobile bases are fleet headquarters that can relocate. They carry everything needed to support major operations.
entries.mnemeNotes: House mobile bases are noble palaces. Hegemony mobile bases are clan fortresses. Guild mobile bases are administrative centers.

entries.definition: A cutter with interchangeable mission pods. Cargo, passenger, fuel, or weapons modules swap in hours.
entries.ceRaw: Modular cutters are the Swiss Army knives of small craft. One hull, infinite missions.
entries.mnemeNotes: The most versatile craft in the Frontier. A single modular cutter can be a cargo hauler in the morning and a gunboat by evening.

entries.definition: Non-jump capital ships designed for static system defense. Immobile fortresses with spinal-mount weapons.
entries.ceRaw: Monitors are system-defense vessels too large for jump drives. They rely on tugs or jump carriers for interstellar movement.
entries.mnemeNotes: The Hegemony clans deploy monitors at warp points and gas giants. Houses use them as mobile star fortresses.

entries.definition: A military fuel tender. Carries refined hydrogen and jump fuel for fleet operations.
entries.ceRaw: Oilers refuel fleets at sea. In space, they carry the hydrogen that makes jump travel possible.
entries.mnemeNotes: Every fleet operation requires oilers. Without them, ships are stranded. House oilers are priority targets in clan wars.

entries.definition: A scheduled mail and passenger vessel operating on fixed routes. Reliable but inflexible.
entries.ceRaw: Packets operate on schedules. They carry mail, passengers, and light cargo between major ports.
entries.mnemeNotes: House packet services are reliable and expensive. Federation packets are subsidized. Frontier packets are irregular and dangerous.

entries.definition: A balanced escort-sized vessel capable of jump travel, patrol, and light combat. The smallest independently-operating starship in most navies.
entries.ceRaw: Corvettes are small starships used for patrol, customs enforcement, and piracy suppression. They carry enough fuel and provisions for short independent missions.
entries.mnemeNotes: The most common ship in the Mneme Variant — patrol corvettes are produced in vast numbers by every polity with a shipyard.

entries.definition: A short-range law enforcement craft. Sensors, communications, and minimal armament.
entries.ceRaw: Patrol craft enforce law in orbital space and planetary approaches. They are the space police.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation patrol craft are standardized. House patrol craft are House-colored. Frontier patrol craft are whatever the local strongman says they are.

entries.definition: A cruiser optimized for law enforcement and piracy suppression. Extended sensors and prisoner facilities.
entries.ceRaw: Patrol cruisers carry marines, detention cells, and advanced sensor suites for tracking smugglers and pirates.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation Patrol Service operates thousands of these. Independent patrol cruisers are common in the Frontier.

entries.definition: A fast, elegant small craft designed for rapid transport of personnel and light cargo. All engines, minimal accommodations.
entries.ceRaw: Pinnaces are fast boats — the yacht or sports car of small craft. They prioritize speed over everything else.
entries.mnemeNotes: Often used by nobles, corporate executives, and smugglers who need to move quickly and discreetly.

entries.definition: The ship's fusion reactor, providing energy for all systems. Must be sized to power M-Drive, J-Drive, weapons, and life support simultaneously.
entries.ceRaw: Power plants are fusion reactors rated by letter code. They require fuel based on their rating and the ship's tonnage.
entries.mnemeNotes: In Mneme, power plants are designated by the same letter code as the M-Drive they support (e.g., Power Plant A supports M-Drive A).

entries.definition: An inmate transport vessel. Secure detention facilities, minimal life support, heavy security.
entries.ceRaw: Prison ships transport convicts between facilities. They are grim places with minimal comforts and maximum security.
entries.mnemeNotes: Guild prison ships are automated and inhumane. House prison ships vary by House morality. Federation prison ships have rehabilitation programs.

entries.definition: A vessel designed for resource extraction surveying. Heavy sensors, sample labs, and claim documentation.
entries.ceRaw: Prospectors evaluate claims. They determine whether a find is worth the investment of a full mining operation.
entries.mnemeNotes: Often converted from old scouts. Guild prospectors have advanced analysis equipment. Independents use whatever they can afford.

entries.definition: An armed merchant vessel disguised as a civilian ship. Concealed weapons revealed only in combat.
entries.ceRaw: Q-ships are warships disguised as merchants. They lure pirates into attacking, then reveal their true nature.
entries.mnemeNotes: Common in House space and the Frontier. Hegemony clans consider Q-ships honorable deception. Guilds consider them terrorism.

entries.definition: A competitive speed craft built for racing. Stripped down, overpowered, and dangerous.
entries.ceRaw: Racing craft are the sports cars of space. They prioritize speed above everything else — including safety.
entries.mnemeNotes: House nobles bet fortunes on racing craft. Federation racing is regulated. Frontier racing is lethal.

entries.definition: A mobile refining platform that processes raw ore into usable materials. Reduces cargo volume by 80%.
entries.ceRaw: Refinery ships process ore in space. They turn low-value rock into high-value refined materials.
entries.mnemeNotes: Guild monopoly on advanced refining. Independent refinery ships use older, less efficient equipment.

entries.definition: A small craft equipped for minor repairs and maintenance. The mechanic's tool kit in space.
entries.ceRaw: Repair skiffs are mobile workshops. They carry tools, spare parts, and a mechanic to fix problems in the field.
entries.mnemeNotes: Common on large ships and stations. A repair skiff can mean the difference between a quick fix and a catastrophic failure.

entries.definition: A mobile workshop and supply vessel capable of repairing starships in the field. Essential for extended fleet operations far from base.
entries.ceRaw: Tenders carry spare parts, machine shops, and engineering crews to maintain a squadron in deep space.
entries.mnemeNotes: Often converted from old freighters. A tender can mean the difference between a fleet returning home or being stranded.

entries.definition: A dedicated search and rescue small craft. Medical equipment, salvage gear, and long-range sensors.
entries.ceRaw: Rescue craft are the emergency vehicles of space. They find and recover survivors from disasters.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation rescue craft are white with red crosses. House rescue craft are House-colored. Frontier rescue craft are independent operators.

entries.definition: A dedicated search and rescue vessel. Medical bays, salvage equipment, and long-range sensors.
entries.ceRaw: Rescue ships find and recover survivors from space disasters. They are the emergency services of the void.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation Rescue Service operates hundreds. Independent rescue ships are often former scouts. Hegemony clans rescue their own; others are left.

entries.definition: A scientific ship equipped with laboratories, sensor arrays, and survey equipment. Payload-dominant design with modest defenses.
entries.ceRaw: Research vessels carry scientists and equipment to study phenomena, survey worlds, and conduct experiments in deep space.
entries.mnemeNotes: The Laboratory Ship and Survey Vessel are classic examples. In Mneme, research vessels are prime targets for corsairs seeking valuable data.

entries.definition: An expedition vessel equipped for hunting, exploration, and wildlife observation on alien worlds.
entries.ceRaw: Safari ships carry hunters, explorers, and scientists to dangerous worlds. They are rugged and well-armed.
entries.mnemeNotes: Popular with House nobles seeking exotic trophies. Federation safari ships are strictly scientific.

entries.definition: A defensive weapon that launches clouds of ablative sand to intercept incoming missiles and energy weapons.
entries.ceRaw: Sand casters are defensive weapons that protect the ship from beam attacks and missiles by deploying clouds of sand.
entries.mnemeNotes: The cheapest and most effective point defense system. Every combatant in the Mneme Variant carries sand casters if it can afford the tonnage.

entries.definition: The standard exploration and message vessel. Fast, self-sufficient, and lightly armed.
entries.ceRaw: Scout/couriers explore the frontier and carry messages between distant worlds. They are the eyes and ears of civilization.
entries.mnemeNotes: The classic Type-S. Every Frontier pilot dreams of owning one. Federation scouts are the most advanced.

entries.definition: A prospecting vessel equipped for resource location and claim staking. Minimal comforts, maximum sensors.
entries.ceRaw: Seekers find valuable resources — minerals, gases, exotic materials. They stake claims and sell the coordinates.
entries.mnemeNotes: The most common first ship for Frontier entrepreneurs. Most fail. A few strike it rich.

entries.definition: A generic small craft carried aboard starships for utility, rescue, and short-range transport. Not a formal naval classification.
entries.ceRaw: Ship's boats are standard equipment on most starships. They provide a means of transport when the main vessel cannot land.
entries.mnemeNotes: In Mneme, 'Ship's Boat' is a catch-all for any small craft under 50 DT carried as auxiliary equipment.

entries.definition: A mixed-use small craft carrying both passengers and cargo. The standard utility craft.
entries.ceRaw: Shuttles are the workhorses of small craft. They carry people, cargo, and anything else that needs moving.
entries.mnemeNotes: Standard equipment on almost every starship. A ship without a shuttle is crippled in port.

entries.definition: An unpowered or minimally powered cargo craft. Towed or pushed by tugs.
entries.ceRaw: Slow boats are unpowered cargo containers with minimal thrusters. They are cheap but helpless.
entries.mnemeNotes: Used for bulk cargo in safe systems. In the Frontier, slow boats are pirate bait.

entries.definition: An unpowered personnel carrier. Towed between ships or from orbit to surface.
entries.ceRaw: Slow pinnaces are unpowered passenger capsules. They are the cheapest way to move people in space.
entries.mnemeNotes: Emergency evacuation craft. Also used for prisoner transfers where escape must be impossible.

entries.definition: A massive weapon running the length of the ship's spine — typically a meson gun, particle accelerator, or railgun. Only mountable on Line Ships and Capitals.
entries.ceRaw: Spinal weapons are the largest ship-mounted weapons. They run the entire length of the vessel and can devastate targets in a single hit.
entries.mnemeNotes: The defining feature of a true capital ship. No Escort or Craft can mount a spinal weapon due to structural and power requirements.

entries.definition: A fast, heavily armed cruiser designed for commerce raiding and deep strikes. Speed + firepower, minimal payload.
entries.ceRaw: Strike cruisers are commerce raiders. They hit hard, take what they can, and run before the fleet arrives.
entries.mnemeNotes: Corsair kings and rogue Houses operate strike cruisers. The Federation considers them pirates regardless of papers.

entries.definition: A merchant vessel (400–600 DT) operating under government subsidy. Carries priority cargo and passengers on fixed routes.
entries.ceRaw: Subsidized merchants receive government support in exchange for carrying mail, passengers, and strategic cargoes on less profitable routes.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation and House subsidized merchants are common. The subsidy comes with strings — priority cargo, military transport clauses.

entries.definition: An extreme-scale battleship exceeding 200,000 DT. Mounts multiple spinal weapons and armor exceeding standard limits.
entries.ceRaw: The largest combat vessel possible. Requires dedicated shipyards and decades of construction.
entries.mnemeNotes: Only the Houses and Guilds have built superdreadnoughts. Most were destroyed in the Collapse Wars.

entries.definition: A capital-scale merchant vessel capable of moving city-sized quantities of cargo. Requires dedicated ports and escorts.
entries.ceRaw: At capital scales, merchant vessels become megafreighters — mobile space stations dedicated to logistics.
entries.mnemeNotes: Rare in the Frontier. Most superfreighters operate on established Core World routes with heavy naval escort.

entries.definition: A vessel equipped for planetary and system survey. Mapping, resource assessment, and habitability studies.
entries.ceRaw: Survey vessels map worlds. They determine whether a planet is worth colonizing, mining, or ignoring.
entries.mnemeNotes: Federation Survey Service operates the largest fleet. Independent surveyors sell data to the highest bidder.

entries.definition: A heavily armed and armored escort designed for static system defense. Lacks jump drives but mounts formidable weapons for its size.
entries.ceRaw: System Defense Boats (SDBs) are non-starships built to defend a single system. They are cheaper than starships and can carry disproportionate firepower.
entries.mnemeNotes: The quintessential Brawler at Escort scale. SDBs are the backbone of planetary defense forces throughout the Mneme Frontier.

entries.definition: A specialized vessel designed to transport fuel and other liquids between systems. Hull is almost entirely fuel tankage.
entries.ceRaw: Tankers are the oilers of space — they refuel fleets and stations far from gas giants or fuel sources.
entries.mnemeNotes: Military tankers are usually escorted. Civilian tankers operate on fixed routes between fuel-rich systems.

entries.definition: A fast, lightly built escort designed to close with enemy ships and deliver torpedo or missile attacks. High speed, high armament, minimal payload.
entries.ceRaw: Torpedo boats are small attack craft optimized for delivering heavy ordnance. They rely on speed and surprise to survive.
entries.mnemeNotes: Popular with corsairs and asymmetric warfare forces. A squadron of torpedo boats can threaten much larger vessels.

entries.definition: Generic term for any cargo-carrying merchant vessel. Covers all sizes and configurations.
entries.ceRaw: Trader is the catch-all term for commercial cargo vessels.
entries.mnemeNotes: In the Frontier, Trader is a profession, not a ship type. Every vessel that carries cargo is a trader.

entries.definition: A large vessel optimized for carrying infantry, vehicles, and landing equipment. A hybrid of Hauler and Support.
entries.ceRaw: Troop transports carry armies. They have extensive barracks, vehicle bays, and drop equipment for planetary assault.
entries.mnemeNotes: Often converted from bulk transports. A troop transport is a prime target — killing one can end a campaign.

entries.definition: A vessel optimized for carrying armies. Barracks, drop equipment, and vehicle bays dominate the hull.
entries.ceRaw: Troop transports carry thousands of soldiers. They are prime targets — killing one can end a campaign.
entries.mnemeNotes: Often converted from bulk transports. The Houses use contracted transports; the Hegemony uses dedicated clan vessels.

entries.definition: A small utility craft for construction and repair work. Manipulator arms, welding torches, and cargo grapples.
entries.ceRaw: Work pods are the construction workers of space. They build, repair, and maintain stations and ships.
entries.mnemeNotes: Essential for any shipyard or construction site. Guild work pods are mass-produced. Independent work pods are often jury-rigged.

entries.definition: An unmanned or minimally crewed express vessel. Automated navigation, pre-programmed routes, minimal life support.
entries.ceRaw: X-boats are automated message carriers. They are cheap, fast, and expendable.
entries.mnemeNotes: The Guilds operate the X-Boat network. Independent X-boats are courier drones. House X-boats carry encrypted diplomatic traffic.

entries.definition: A privately-owned vessel designed for luxury travel and entertainment. High payload dedicated to passenger comfort.
entries.ceRaw: Yachts are the pleasure craft of the wealthy — fast, comfortable, and often heavily customized.
entries.mnemeNotes: Nobles, corporate executives, and retired admirals favor yachts. They are rarely armed but often armored against piracy.
